defect.description: The edge case where new_mobject is old_mobject: the new deduplication removes the object from the list before searching, so scene.replace(a, a) no longer finds a, raises ValueError and leaves a removed from the scene; the deduplication must skip the case new_m is old_m (or run only after the replacement).
defect.location: src/scene.py (the deduplication at the top of replace_in_list)

review_items: Dedup guard removes new_m from every list the recursion visits, corrupting unrelated groups
replace(obj, obj) removes the object because the guard removes it before the search; ValueError and object lost
Guard strips new_m from groups containing both new_m and old_m at the same level
Dedup guard placed at the wrong depth; should only check the list where the replacement occurs
remove() only removes the first occurrence when duplicates exist
Tests only cover old_m and new_m in the same list; cross-group bug untested
Missing test for replace(obj, obj), which the guard corrupts
votes.evidence_quote: replace(obj, obj) — replacing an object with itself — removes that object from the scene because the guard removes it before the search finds it
votes.justification: The second finding reports the exact defect at the dedup guard in src/scene.py: the guard removes the object before the search, so the search fails, ValueError is raised, and the object is gone from the scene. The last item restates the same defect as a missing test.
